title: Stuff vs Staff, Will vs Would, Near vs Close to

vocabulary.note_ar: تُنطق /stʌf/ مثل tough و bluff، وهي غير معدودة
vocabulary.note_en: Pronounced /stʌf/, like tough and bluff. Uncountable.
vocabulary.example: Whose stuff is this on the table?

vocabulary.meaning_en: to push something into a space quickly, without order
vocabulary.example: He stuffed his clothes into the bag.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the people who work in an office, shop or restaurant
vocabulary.example: The restaurant staff were very friendly.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a long stick that helps a person walk
vocabulary.example: The old man walked with a staff.
My tutor helps me with grammar.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to pretend you will do something or have something
near (distance); about (number); having a strong relationship with
vocabulary.example: The bank is close to my house.

vocabulary.meaning_en: not far from; (verb) to come closer
vocabulary.example: The school is near the park. / The day is nearing.
Close to 15 people came; it's an approximate number.
There is a strong bond between them.

fine_lines.title: stuff vs staff
fine_lines.explanation_ar: stuff /ʌ/ = أشياء عامة (أو يحشر). staff /æ/ = الموظفون الذين يعملون أو يقدمون المساعدة. الفرق الأكبر في النطق: uh مقابل ah.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Stuff /ʌ/ = general things (or to push in). Staff /æ/ = the people who work or offer help. The big difference is the sound: "uh" vs "ah".

examples.sentence: Please take your stuff off my desk.
The hotel staff helped us with our bags.

fine_lines.title: will vs would
fine_lines.explanation_ar: will = وعد أو مستقبل حقيقي نؤمن أنه سيحدث. would = متخيَّل أو مشروط، لا وعد فيه. إذا قلت If I won a million dollars فقل I would buy... وليس I will buy.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Will = a promise or a real future we believe in. Would = imaginary or conditional, no promise. If you say "If I won a million dollars", say "I would buy...", not "I will buy".

examples.sentence: If I won a million dollars, I would buy a house. (imaginary)

fine_lines.title: near vs close to (not "near to")
fine_lines.explanation_ar: يقول جيمس: لا تجمع بينهما فتقول near to؛ قل near أو close to. close to تعني أيضًا: حوالي (للأعداد) وعلاقة قوية. near يمكن أن تكون فعلًا (يقترب).
fine_lines.explanation_en: James says: don't mix them into "near to"; say near or close to. Close to also means about (numbers) and a strong relationship. Near can also be a verb (come closer).

examples.sentence: My house is near the station.
He is very close to his mother.

expressions.meaning_en: Who do these things belong to?
expressions.example: Whose stuff is this on the floor?
Close to 15 people came to the meeting.
As the day drew near, we got more excited.
He says he'll quit, but he's just bluffing.

grammar.title: Stuff: uncountable noun and verb
grammar.explanation_ar: stuff كاسم غير معدود لأشياء كثيرة (my stuff وليس a stuff). وكفعل: stuff something into something.
grammar.explanation_en: Stuff as a noun is uncountable for many things (my stuff, not a stuff). As a verb: stuff something into something.
examples: She stuffed the papers into her bag.

grammar.title: Will for promises and the future; would for imaginary conditions
grammar.explanation_ar: will + المصدر: وعد أو مستقبل حقيقي. If + ماضٍ ... would + المصدر: حالة متخيلة مشروطة.
grammar.explanation_en: will + base verb: a promise or a real future. If + past ... would + base verb: an imaginary condition.
examples: I will go to the store in five minutes.
If I saved a dollar a day, I would have a million dollars in a million days.

grammar.title: Close to vs near
grammar.explanation_ar: close to: (1) حوالي للكمية، (2) علاقة عاطفية قوية، (3) مسافة قريبة. near: مسافة أو وقت قريب، ويمكن أن تكون فعلًا. لا تقل near to؛ قل near.
grammar.explanation_en: Close to: (1) about, for quantity; (2) a strong emotional relationship; (3) a short distance. Near: a short distance or time; it can also be a verb. Don't say "near to"; say near.
examples: She is close to her sister.
